subject: Certified erasure metrics and geofallback language - DPA redlines
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmehealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-04-25T09:12:00+01:00
Subject: Questions on certified erasure metrics + fallback to on-prem clause

Hi Laura,

Thanks for sending the DPA draft. Our security team flagged two items we need clearer commitments on before procurement can advance: 

1) "Certified erasure metrics" — the draft references a certificate once data is deleted, but we need a short, operational definition (what logs or evidence you will provide, and within what timeframe). Do you produce a signed certification (PDF) per deletion request or a proof bundle (audit log + tombstone)?

2) Geofallback/on-prem fallback — we have a requirement that, in the event of a region outage or legal hold, Redwood must be able to initiate an on-prem transfer or isolated processing for a defined narrow set of data. Is that something you can commit to as an optional schedule/appendix, and if so, how do you limit retention during the fallback?

High level asks: concrete deliverables and timelines we can reference in the DPA (e.g., cert within X days, evidence schema link, maximum retention on cache components). Can you and your legal/ops teams propose language?

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of InfoSec, Acme Health

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-25T15:48:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Questions on certified erasure metrics + fallback to on-prem clause

Elena —

Thanks, and appreciated the clear asks. Quick summary of what we can propose and attached a short spec: redwood-certified-erasure-spec.pdf. High-level: 

- Certified erasure deliverable: we provide a signed PDF "Erasure Certificate" containing:
  - request id, target dataset, timestamp of deletion initiation, deletion completion timestamp, SHA256 of deleted object list (where applicable), and a reference to the retention policy that triggered the deletion.
  - We will include an audit-log bundle (obfuscated request traces) for compliance reviews if requested under NDA.
  - Target delivery: within 10 business days of completion.

- Evidence format and schema: we reference an internal JSON schema (included in links) used to generate the certificate. If Acme has a preferred schema, we can map fields one-to-one.

- Ephemeral/cache components: for KV/prefix caches and inference telemetry we propose explicit limits in the DPA appendix: default TTL 48 hours for ephemeral caches, with a maximum allowed mis-retention window of 72 hours in exceptional cases where a cache flush was delayed due to an operational incident. We will commit to proof of flush (cache tombstone markers + replayable eviction logs) in the certificate.

- Geofallback/on-prem: operationally we can support a scheduled on-prem transfer for a narrow set of datasets under a separate addendum (Private Deployment Appendix). The addendum will include: a transfer plan, timeline (typically 7–14 business days to provision and transfer), and a retention cap during the fallback (no more than 30 days unless extended by mutual written agreement).

Karthik and Marissa are looped for redline and ops validation. If that aligns with Acme's ask, we can produce a redline for the DPA with these points codified.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Product, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-certified-erasure-spec.pdf (pdf)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-26T08:26:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Questions on certified erasure metrics + fallback to on-prem clause

Elena / Laura —

Thanks for the summary. A few legal redline suggestions and clarifying questions before we push a formal DPA edit: 

1) Delivery timing: Laura's 10-business-day window for the certificate is reasonable; request that we add a clause that the clock starts on deletion completion (not initiation), and that force majeure pauses the clock. 

2) Scope of evidence: Acme asked for "audit-log bundle (obfuscated request traces)" — need to be explicit that the bundle excludes unrelated customer data and that Redwood will only provide logs relevant to the deletion request id. Also propose adding an accepted evidence size cap (e.g., 50MB) and an escalation channel if larger bundles are needed.

3) Definition of "tombstone marker": for DPA clarity, define as a non-recoverable deletion flag written to audit storage with a hash pointer. This avoids open-ended phrasing.

4) Geofallback trigger and cost: we can include geofallback as an optional Appendix but must also add a line that operationalization may require a one-time provisioning fee for on-prem staging and that specific SLAs (latency/throughput) are out of scope unless otherwise agreed. 

If acceptable, we'll prepare dpa-redline-20280427.docx with tracked changes. Also tagging Marissa: please confirm the 48/72h cache windows and provide a short playbook for proof artifacts (eviction logs, cache TTL markers).

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-04-26T11:03:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Questions on certified erasure metrics + fallback to on-prem clause

Karthik, Laura —

This looks promising. A few follow-ups from procurement/security: 

- The 10 business days is acceptable if the certificate includes the full audit bundle (we might need the ability to request extended evidence in exceptional investigations). Please add a clause that allows Acme to request expanded evidence within a 30-day window after the certificate delivery (forensic review), with Redwood's commitment to respond within a further 10 business days and an estimate of cost if the bundle exceeds the size cap.

- For geofallback: procurement requests a high-level cost estimate for on-prem provisioning to include in our budget. If you can provide a standard T-shirt estimate (S/M/L) with ballpark costs that would be helpful.

Can you attach the redline and the playbook so our security folks can review?

Thanks,
Elena

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmehealth.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-27T09:17:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Questions on certified erasure metrics + fallback to on-prem clause

Elena —

Attaching the operational playbook (playbook-erase-steps.xlsx) and a short note on proof artifacts. Key points from ops: 

- Cache eviction proof: we emit a tombstone event which is immutably logged to our audit pipeline. The event contains: key prefix, deletion request id, TTL expiry vs explicit eviction timestamp (if eviction triggered), and a SHA256 snapshot of the evicted keys list (where applicable).

- Telemetry retention: inference telemetry used for debugging is rolled up daily and persisted only to a separate telemetry shard. By policy we redact PII at ingest and expire raw telemetry within 14 days; aggregated metrics are retained up to 365 days. For DPA purposes we can agree to an additional contractual cap that commits to expiring raw telemetry within 30 days for Acme's tenant.

- Proof delivery mechanics: the Erasure Certificate will contain a signed link to a time-bound S3 bundle (access-controlled) with the audit artifacts; we will retain access links for 30 days by default and can extend on request.

I'll also add a short section on the playbook describing the steps for on-prem transfer choreography.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachment: playbook-erase-steps.xlsx (xlsx)

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-27T11:04:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Questions on certified erasure metrics + fallback to on-prem clause

Elena / Procurement team —

Thanks all. Next steps: 

1) Redwood will send a tracked redline (dpa-redline-20280427.docx) by EOD 2028-04-27 with: the certificate definition, 10-business-day delivery window (clock starts at deletion completion), evidence size cap and escalation path, tombstone definition, TTL limits for caches, and a geofallback Appendix with rough T-shirt cost estimates.

2) Marissa will add the playbook section for on-prem choreography and the telemetry retention cap (30 days for raw telemetry) to the attachment.

3) Acme to review redline + playbook; procurement to confirm whether the 7–14 day provisioning window and the T-shirt estimate are acceptable for budgeting.

If that timeline works I will also include a one-paragraph summary suitable for the legal appendix so procurement can paste it into the purchase order.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Product, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachment: dpa-redline-20280427.docx (docx)
